saints.name: St. Delphinus
saints.title: Bishop of Bordeaux
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop of Bordeaux who baptized St. Paulinus of Nola and opposed the Priscillian heresy…
biography: Delphinus was bishop of Bordeaux in Aquitaine in the last decades of the fourth century. In 380 he attended the Council of Saragossa, where bishops of Spain and Aquitaine condemned the errors of Priscillian, and in 384 a synod in his own city of Bordeaux deposed the Priscillianist bishop Instantius.

He corresponded with St. Ambrose of Milan, who wrote to him on the affairs of the troubled churches. When Pontius Paulinus, the rich senator of Bordeaux and future St. Paulinus of Nola, sought baptism, it was Delphinus who baptized him, together with his brother, about the year 389.

Paulinus revered him ever after as a father in God, writing to him from Spain and Nola with filial affection, and the presbyter Amandus, his successor, continued the care of the convert. Delphinus died about 403 and is named in the Roman Martyrology on 24 December; he is honoured as patron of Bordeaux, the see he governed through the Priscillianist storms.
saints.knownFor: Baptizing St. Paulinus of Nola and opposing Priscillianism.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
